question_set_contract.dependency_contract: At the module boundary q01 retrieves Lesson 3 graph knowledge and q07 combines the earlier module's loading and extension knowledge with current stress-strain calculations.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: definitions and ratios to circular-area stress and integrated stress-strain calculation

questions.prompt: On a force-extension graph, state how to recognise the proportional region and state what the gradient represents when force is vertical.
Define tensile stress and tensile strain.
Which is the SI unit of stress?
A wire’s extension and original length are both measured in millimetres. Which statement about strain is correct?

options.A: The values cannot be used until both are converted to metres.
options.B: The ratio is dimensionless because the identical units cancel.
options.D: Final length must be used in the denominator.

questions.prompt: Two wires carry the same tensile force. Wire X has half the cross-sectional area of wire Y. How do their stresses compare?

options.A: X has half the stress of Y.
options.B: X has twice the stress of Y.

questions.prompt: A circular wire of diameter 1.20 mm carries a tensile force of 90.0 N. Calculate its cross-sectional area and tensile stress. State the unit of stress and one physical check on the result.

figure.purpose: Assess selecting the perpendicular circular cross-section and radius
figure.brief: Original black-and-white wire with outward arrows and a separate circular end view labelled diameter 1.20 mm. Do not show radius, area formula or answer.
figure.alt_text: A tensile wire has a circular end view with diameter 1.20 mm.

questions.prompt: A wire has original length 1.50 m and diameter 0.60 mm. Outward end forces of 36.0 N increase its length to 1.5030 m. Classify the loading, calculate the extension, cross-sectional area, stress and strain, and explain why strain has no unit.

figure.purpose: Assess integration of prior loading/extension with new stress and strain
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired before-and-after wire diagram with outward arrows, original/final lengths and diameter. Include no classification, extension bracket, formula or result.
figure.alt_text: A wire lengthens under outward forces with lengths and diameter labelled.
